tagline: Leading integrated energy company providing natural gas and electricity supply across Spain and Europe
hero_kpi_rationale: Naturgy's long-term natural gas purchase commitments of €45.3 Bn reflect its strategic positioning as a major energy distributor in Europe, exposed to critical contracts securing natural gas and LNG supply.

kpis.name: Unbilled Revenue (Energy Supplied)
kpis.explanation: Amount of revenue recognized for energy supplied but not yet billed to end customers.
kpis.description: Amount of revenue recognized for energy supplied but not yet billed to end customers as of December 31, 2024. This estimate is based on internal models comparing meter readings with management data, multiplied by contractual tariffs.
kpis.signal: Estimation of energy consumption between the last meter reading and fiscal year-end.

kpis.name: Property, Plant and Equipment
kpis.explanation: Value of tangible assets required for energy and distribution operations.
kpis.description: Value of property, plant and equipment (land, buildings, facilities, equipment) consolidated as of December 31, 2024, subject to annual impairment testing under IFRS-EU.
kpis.signal: High amount reflecting a capital-intensive industry with complex physical infrastructure.

kpis.name: Intangible Assets and Goodwill
kpis.explanation: Value of non-physical assets including goodwill, patents, and commercial rights.
kpis.description: Consolidated intangible assets, including goodwill, subject to annual impairment tests under IFRS-EU, as of December 31, 2024.
kpis.signal: Significant intangible assets, primarily goodwill from historical acquisitions.

kpis.name: Right-of-Use Assets (IFRS 16 Leases)
kpis.explanation: Value of assets related to lease contracts (premises, equipment, facilities) recognized under IFRS 16.
kpis.description: Right-of-use assets recognized under IFRS 16 for land, building, and equipment lease contracts, as of December 31, 2024.
kpis.signal: Presence of significant lease contracts capitalized on balance sheet in accordance with current accounting standards.

kpis.name: Natural Gas and LNG Purchase Commitments
kpis.explanation: Total amount of long-term contracts for the purchase of natural gas and liquefied natural gas.
kpis.description: Long-term contractual commitments for the purchase of natural gas and liquefied natural gas (LNG), classified as own-use contracts and excluded from the scope of IFRS 9, as of December 31, 2024.
kpis.signal: Massive contractual exposure to energy markets, covering short, medium, and long-term forecasted gas supply needs.

kpis.name: Net Asset Impairment Losses
kpis.explanation: Net amount of asset impairments recognized in the income statement.
kpis.description: Asset impairments (PP&E, intangibles, right-of-use) recognized in 2024 profit after cash-generating unit analysis under IFRS-EU.
kpis.signal: Limited impairment losses (€52 M) more than offset by impairment reversals (€70 M), reflecting an overall improvement in asset values.

kpis.name: Total Assets
kpis.description: Total assets extracted from yfinance over the last 4 years.
kpis.signal: Total assets of €39.1 Bn in the latest year

kpis.name: Total Debt
kpis.description: Total debt extracted from yfinance over the last 4 years.
kpis.signal: Total debt of €16.75 Bn in the latest year

risks.title: Dependence on Public Energy Regulation
risks.score_rationale: The risk ranks at the top of risk factors (equivalent to Item 1A), mentioned with strong language ("subject to regulatory decisions", "significant impact"). It is stable over time and represents a core category for Naturgy's regulated energy business.

risks.title: Increased Competition in Liberalized Markets
risks.score_rationale: The risk is explicitly mentioned in the notes, with moderate to strong language ("intense competition", "margin pressure"). It is rising due to new market entrants. Competition is a key driver in energy retail segments.

risks.title: Exposure to Latin American Energy Policies
risks.score_rationale: The risk is prominently positioned in the notes, with concerned language ("political instability", "unilateral government measures"). It is increasing due to recent tensions in certain countries. The region represents a significant portion of international operations.

risks.title: Cybersecurity of Critical Infrastructure
risks.score_rationale: The risk is mentioned indirectly but critically in the context of energy networks. The language is alarming ("targeted attacks", "service disruption"). It is consistently rising. This category is strategic for modern utilities.

risks.title: Dependence on Strategic Gas Suppliers
risks.score_rationale: The risk is clearly identified in the notes (natural gas supply). Firm language ("supply concentration", "potential disruption"). Stable but critical. The sector heavily relies on the natural gas supply chain.

risks.title: Risks Related to the Energy Transition
risks.score_rationale: The risk is central in the document, mentioned with strong language ("decarbonization", "growing regulatory obligations"). Consistently rising. A strategic category for the group's future.

risks.title: Regulatory Disputes and International Arbitrations
risks.score_rationale: The risk is documented in the notes (ongoing arbitrations). Cautious language ("uncertain outcome", "significant amounts at stake"). Stable but recurring. Disputes are frequent in international concessions.

ai_positioning.summary: No mention of artificial intelligence or related technologies in the provided documents.
evidence: No reference to AI in the audit report.
Absence of KPIs related to digital innovation or automation.
Business model focused on physical energy and infrastructure.
